# Install Script Reference

The POSIX shell one-liner that installs the `glassfrog` CLI on a Linux or macOS host: its invocation forms, configuration variables, supported platforms, integrity verification, install location, and failure modes.

> **🚧 Not yet available — planned.** This documents the *specified* installer (spec 027). The `install.sh` script is **not yet present in the repository** and the automated release pipeline that publishes the archives it downloads has not shipped, so the one-liners below do **not work today** — running them currently fails (the raw URL 404s). This page describes the intended mechanism so the design is reviewable; treat it as forthcoming until the install script and a published release exist. For installing today, build from source with the Go toolchain (`go install github.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog@latest`).

## Overview

The installer is specified as a single POSIX shell script, `install.sh`, to be hosted at the repository root and invoked over the network as a one-liner. It detects the host OS and architecture, resolves a release, downloads the matching archive and the checksums file, verifies the archive's integrity, and installs the binary into a per-user directory. It adds no command to the CLI, requires no runtime or package manager, and never escalates privileges (no `sudo`).

Because the hosted URL points at the `main`-branch raw content, the one-liner always resolves the newest stable release and therefore doubles as the upgrade path.

## Invocation

| Form | Command |
|---|---|
| Default (curl) | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog/main/install.sh \| sh` |
| Default (wget) | `wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog/main/install.sh \| sh` |
| With configuration | `curl -fsSL <url> \| GLASSFROG_VERSION=v1.3.0 GLASSFROG_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/bin" sh` |

Configuration is supplied through environment variables only, not flags. The variables must be set on the `sh` invocation (the right side of the pipe), as shown above — not before `curl`.

## Configuration

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GLASSFROG_VERSION` | no | _(latest stable)_ | Release to install. A tag, with or without the leading `v` (`v1.3.0` or `1.3.0`). Unset installs the latest **stable** release (pre-releases excluded). A pinned tag installs that exact release, **including** a pre-release. |
| `GLASSFROG_INSTALL_DIR` | no | `${XDG_BIN_HOME:-$HOME/.local/bin}` | Directory the binary is installed into. Created if absent. Must be writable by the user — the script never escalates privileges. |
| `GLASSFROG_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL` | no | `https://github.com` | Base URL for release resolution and downloads. **Distinct from the CLI's `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL`** (the API endpoint) — exporting the API override does not redirect installer downloads. |

No other input is read. Platform, asset names, and the checksum algorithm are derived or fixed, never configured. The three variables share the `GLASSFROG_` prefix for discoverability but are semantically separate from the runtime CLI's environment (`GLASSFROG_BASE_URL`, `GLASSFROG_TOKEN`, `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT`), none of which the installer reads.

## Supported Platforms

Platform is detected from `uname` and mapped to the published asset names. Only the following are supported:

| Axis | Detected values | Mapped to |
|---|---|---|
| OS (`uname -s`) | `Darwin` | `darwin` |
| OS (`uname -s`) | `Linux` | `linux` |
| Architecture (`uname -m`) | `x86_64`, `amd64` | `amd64` |
| Architecture (`uname -m`) | `arm64`, `aarch64` | `arm64` |

The supported set is `darwin`/`linux` × `amd64`/`arm64`. Any other OS (for example Windows) or architecture is rejected before any download.

## Required Tooling

The script probes for the required tools before downloading. If a category has no usable tool, the script fails with an actionable message naming the missing tool (exit 2, before any download).

| Category | Accepted tools (in order) |
|---|---|
| Downloader | `curl` (preferred), else `wget` |
| Checksum | `sha256sum`, else `shasum -a 256`, else `openssl dgst -sha256` |
| Archive | `tar` |

## What the Script Does

1. **Detect platform** from `uname -s` and `uname -m`; reject an unsupported OS or architecture (exit 2).
2. **Detect tooling**; if no downloader or no checksum tool is available, fail before downloading (exit 2).
3. **Resolve the tag.** With no `GLASSFROG_VERSION`, it requests `${GLASSFROG_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL}/Luscii/cli-glassfrog/releases/latest` and reads the resolved tag from the redirect. With `GLASSFROG_VERSION` set, it uses that value as the tag verbatim.
4. **Construct asset names** from the resolved tag. With `<ver>` being the tag without its leading `v`:
   - Archive: `glassfrog_<ver>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz`
   - Checksums: `glassfrog_<ver>_checksums.txt`
   - Download base: `${GLASSFROG_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL}/Luscii/cli-glassfrog/releases/download/<tag>/<name>` (the download path uses the tag as published, carrying `v`).
5. **Download** the archive and the checksums file into a temporary directory (`mktemp -d`, cleaned on exit via a trap).
6. **Verify** the archive's sha256 against its line in the checksums file. On mismatch, nothing is installed (exit 3).
7. **Extract and install.** Only a verified binary is moved into `GLASSFROG_INSTALL_DIR` (overwriting any existing binary — this is the upgrade behavior). Nothing touches the install directory before verification passes.
8. **Report success** to stdout: the install path and the installed version, e.g. `Installed glassfrog v1.3.0 to /home/u/.local/bin/glassfrog`.
9. **PATH guidance.** If `GLASSFROG_INSTALL_DIR` is not on `$PATH`, the script prints the exact line to add it (e.g. `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`). It never edits shell profiles.

## Integrity Verification

All download, verification, and extraction happen in a temporary directory. The archive's sha256 is verified against its entry in the downloaded checksums file. Only a verified binary is moved into the install directory. On a checksum mismatch, no binary is written to the target location, the temporary directory is cleaned, and the script exits 3. Every non-zero exit leaves the install directory unchanged — there is no partial binary.

## Version Normalization

A pinned `GLASSFROG_VERSION` is accepted with or without the `v` prefix and normalized internally: the download path uses the tag exactly as the release publishes it (carrying `v`), while the asset name uses `<ver>` without `v`. The tag resolved from the `latest` redirect already carries the published form.

## Idempotence and Upgrade

Re-running installs the resolved version over any existing binary at the target path. Running with no `GLASSFROG_VERSION` upgrades to the newest stable release; pinning an older tag downgrades. The operation converges — no duplicate state and no partial leftovers, because the temporary directory is always cleaned.

## Exit Codes

The installer defines its own small exit-code scheme, distinct from the CLI's runtime convention. Where they overlap, they agree: 0 = success, 2 = usage.

| Code | Meaning | Triggering conditions |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Success | Binary verified and installed. |
| 1 | Runtime failure | Download/network error, missing release asset (404), extraction failure, filesystem error writing the install directory. |
| 2 | Usage / environment error | Unsupported OS or architecture; no usable downloader or checksum tool; malformed `GLASSFROG_VERSION`; install directory not creatable. |
| 3 | Integrity failure | The archive's sha256 does not match its entry in the checksums file. |

## Failure Modes

| Condition | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Unsupported platform (Windows, unsupported arch) | stderr message naming the detected `os`/`arch` and the supported set (`darwin`/`linux` × `amd64`/`arm64`); nothing installed; exit 2. |
| No downloader / no sha256 tool | stderr message naming which tool category is missing and what satisfies it; exit 2, before any download. |
| Latest cannot be resolved | No stable release exists, or the redirect yields no tag → stderr message; exit 1. |
| Pinned version not found | Asset download returns 404 → stderr message naming the version and asset; nothing installed; exit 1. |
| Download failure (network/transient) | stderr message; temporary directory cleaned; nothing installed; exit 1. |
| Checksum mismatch | stderr message naming the integrity failure; **no binary written** to the install directory; temporary directory cleaned; exit 3. |
| Install directory not on `$PATH` | **Not an error** — install succeeds (exit 0); stdout reports success and prints the exact `export PATH=…` line. |

All diagnostics go to stderr; only the success report (path and version) goes to stdout.

## Related Acquisition Channels

A Homebrew tap and an npm wrapper are **planned** as additional routes to the same released binary, but neither ships today — there is no `brews:` section in the repo's GoReleaser config and no npm package yet. Like the install script itself, they depend on the automated release pipeline that has not yet shipped. When available, they will install the same upstream artifacts by other means, independently of this script.
